title: Failures and Resilience in the IP Era: Navigating the Fragility of Modern Telecommunications Networks—The Sovereign Functions
authors: Raymond Owen; Adam Bryant; Leigh Finch; Daniel Franklin; Mahrokh Abdollahi; Mehran Abolhasan
summary: Failure-centric survey arguing that large telecom outages often originate in shared IP-level functions (routing, naming, time sync) and supporting services (authentication, licensing, configuration) rather than in physical redundancy gaps.
data_or_testbed: public outage reports and case studies
key_result: Organises real-world outages around interdependent 'sovereign' and supporting functions and derives mitigation directions and their economic consequences.
limitation_or_critique: Qualitative and IP-network-wide; it does not model 5GC NF failover, subscriber-database replication or AI-based assurance.

title: Residual Artifact Governance With ML-Enabled Garbage Collection Prediction in Kubernetes-Based 5G/6G Service-Based Architecture
authors: Larisa-Mihaela Tufeanu; Marius-Constantin Vochin; Frank Y. Li
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Proposes a master-agent add-on to a Kubernetes-hosted SBA core that learns cleanup policies for leftover cluster objects and predicts when their build-up will destabilise the cluster.
method: ML time-to-collapse prediction plus bounded, periodic fractional garbage collection by per-NF agents
data_or_testbed: Kubernetes-based SBA prototype under nominal and stress leak regimes
key_result: Shows that residual-artifact accumulation can be measured, forecast and kept bounded with Kubernetes-native mechanisms without modifying the core NFs.
limitation_or_critique: Targets a platform-level ageing problem rather than NF or procedure failures, and is validated on a prototype only, without operator workloads.

title: A Dynamic UPF Fault Recovery Mechanism for Enhanced Resilience in 5G Core Networks
authors: Shirin Behnaminia; Pardis Yavari; Zeinab Zali; Mohammad Reza Heidarpour
summary: Adds UPF failure detection, application-layer PDU session restoration and failure-history-aware UPF selection to an OpenAirInterface core.
method: heartbeat-based failure detection, session restoration, failure-aware UPF selection
data_or_testbed: OpenAirInterface 5GC with TCP and UDP traffic
key_result: Restores connectivity within a few seconds after a UPF failure with low packet loss.
limitation_or_critique: Recent preprint, single-site lab; not compared with standard SMF-driven PFCP restoration in TS 23.527.

title: AnomalyTrack: Scalable and Self-Adaptive Anomaly Detection in Large-Scale 5G Networks
authors: Michel Santos Da Silva; Adriano Guilherme Silva Rocha; Lourenco Alves Pereira
venue: 2025 IEEE Symposium on Computers and Communications (ISCC)
summary: Presents a self-adapting KPI anomaly-detection framework for 5G SA networks that combines density-based outlier detectors and seasonal time-series models, and specifies where it runs in the core and what it costs.
method: unsupervised outlier detection (LOF, COF, IF-LOF) plus ARIMA/SARIMA forecasting
data_or_testbed: one year of KPI data from a commercial mobile operator (over half a million KPI series)
key_result: Reports about 97% detection accuracy with inference within a few seconds per 30-minute batch, much faster than the operator's conventional monitoring.
limitation_or_critique: Detection only, on aggregated KPIs; no root-cause localisation, no link to NWDAF/MDA interfaces and no closed-loop action.

title: Autonomic Closed-Loop Service Management based on Interworking Multiple AI Models
authors: Takahiro Hirayama-; Masahiro Jibiki; Takuya Miyasaka; Minato Sakuraba; Junichi Kawasaki; Satoshi Akabori; Takayuki Kuroda
venue: NOMS 2025-2025 IEEE Network Operations and Management Symposium
summary: Defines a unified interface through which several AI models (self-monitoring, self-configuration, self-optimisation) cooperate to run closed-loop management of cloud-native network functions, including reacting to predicted failures.
method: interworking of three AI models in an autonomic closed loop with failure prediction
key_result: The prototype builds network services automatically and keeps the QoS of running services by acting on past and predicted failure events.
limitation_or_critique: Prototype description with little quantitative evaluation; not mapped to 3GPP actuators such as NF reselection or TS 23.527 restoration.
standards_link: ETSI ZSM 009 (closed loops); TS 28.535/28.536 (assurance closed loop)

title: A Scalable and Fault-Tolerant 5G Core on Kubernetes
authors: Sourav Paul; Tanvi Keluskar; Mythili Vutukuru
venue: 2025 17th International Conference on COMmunication Systems and NETworks (COMSNETS)
summary: Starts from a production-grade 3GPP-compliant core and builds several cloud-native variants that use Kubernetes failover and auto-scaling differently, then compares their scalability and resilience.
method: design-space comparison of cloud-native 5GC variants on Kubernetes
key_result: Exposes measurable trade-offs between performance, fault tolerance and cloud overhead, with guidance on which design choices to adopt.
limitation_or_critique: Single-cluster study; geo-redundant sites, subscriber-database failover and AI-driven decisions are outside its scope.

title: ForenSiX: Automated Network Forensics and Diagnostics for Beyond-5G and 6G Networks Using Large Language Models
authors: Xuanbo Huang; Kaiping Xue; Lutong Chen; Jiangping Han; Jian Li; David S. L. Wei
summary: Combines a data-dependency graph derived statically from standards, NF source code and configuration with LLM-assisted log tracking to locate root causes of subscriber-visible failures across core NFs.
method: static dependency-graph construction plus regex and off-the-shelf LLM log analysis
key_result: Demonstrates automated tracing of faults across multiple NFs in realistic scenarios with good reliability and adaptability (qualitative in the abstract).
limitation_or_critique: Magazine-style evaluation on an open-source lab; no public benchmark, accuracy against baselines or LLM error analysis is reported in the abstract.

title: Proactive 5G Core Network Failure Prediction using Nonlinear Dynamical Analysis and Statistical Outlier Detection
authors: Pragadeeswari Selvakumar; Marius Corici; Arun Prakash; Marcus Purat
summary: Studies the dynamics of 5GC control-plane metrics with phase-space reconstruction and, finding no chaos, predicts failures by tracking the density of Mahalanobis-distance outliers.
method: Takens embedding and Lyapunov analysis, then hypersphere/Mahalanobis outlier-density thresholding
data_or_testbed: control-plane metrics from a 5G core testbed
key_result: Rising outlier density is a lightweight early-warning signal of failure risk, suitable for real-time use (no accuracy figure in the abstract).
limitation_or_critique: Workshop paper with threshold-based alarms; no localisation of the faulty NF and no comparison with learned detectors.

title: Evaluating CAP Theorem on a Stateless 5G Core
authors: Siddhesh Pratim Sovitkar; Shwetha Vittal; Antony Franklin A
summary: Measures the consistency-versus-availability trade-off of a 3GPP-compliant stateless 5GC whose NFs share an external state store, running it in CP and AP modes under network partition.
method: testbed experiments comparing CP and AP operating modes of the shared state store
key_result: CP mode completes more PDU session establishments correctly but is less available than AP mode, quantifying the CAP trade-off for core state.
limitation_or_critique: Short paper on a single site; it does not consider cross-site (geo-redundant) replication, failover time or the effect on UE retries.

title: 5GC-Analyser: Demistifying the 5G Core Network Through Statistical Analysis
authors: Abderaouf Khichane; Ilhem Fajjari; Nadjib Aitsaadi; Mourad Gueroui
venue: ICC 2024 - IEEE International Conference on Communications
summary: Statistically analyses dependencies and causal links among the metrics of 5GC microservices to decide which observability techniques suit online monitoring of the core.
method: statistical correlation and causality analysis of NF/microservice metrics
data_or_testbed: cloud-native 5GC with simulated users replaying conditions observed on an operator's (Orange) gNBs
key_result: Reveals inter-NF metric dependencies that inform the choice of online observability and proactive degradation detection methods.
limitation_or_critique: Exploratory analysis without a deployed detector or RCA benchmark; the results are a basis for later work rather than a closed loop.

title: Congestion Control by Mobile Core and RAN Coordination in 5G Mobile Network
authors: Takuya Kato; Takuya Miyasaka; Atsushi Tagami
summary: Addresses the reconnection storm after large-scale failures by letting an orchestration platform, rather than an overloaded AMF, compute traffic-reduction rates applied at base stations.
method: RAN-core coordinated congestion control computed by the orchestrator
key_result: Recovery converges within about 9% of the theoretical limit, and the paper lists gaps in 3GPP and O-RAN specifications for implementing the scheme.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only; UE behaviour is modelled at aggregate level, without NAS timers or per-procedure outcomes.
standards_link: TS 23.501 (AMF overload control); TS 24.501 (NAS back-off); O-RAN

title: LOCOMOTIVE 5G Core for 6G ready Resilient and Highly Available Network Slices and SFCs
authors: Sourav Sarkar; Shwetha Vittal; Antony Franklin A
venue: 2022 18th International Conference on Network and Service Management (CNSM)
summary: Designs a resilient load-balancing layer for the 5GC control plane, built with XDP/eBPF, and compares it with classic hot-standby redundancy under overload and load-balancer failure.
method: eBPF/XDP-based load balancer with active-active redundancy
key_result: Serves at least 16% more control-plane requests under overload, drops 22% fewer during load-balancer failure and gains about 4% availability over hot standby.
limitation_or_critique: Single-site evaluation focused on the load balancer; no learning component and no cross-site or database failover.

title: PP5GS—An Efficient Procedure-Based and Stateless Architecture for Next-Generation Core Networks
authors: Endri Goshi; Raffael Stahl; Hasanin Harkous; Mu He; Rastin Pries; Wolfgang Kellerer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Re-decomposes the 5GC into stateless per-procedure NFs that keep UE context externally, to cut inter-NF signalling and simplify orchestration.
method: procedure-based functional decomposition with external state; Kubernetes deployment
data_or_testbed: private cloud orchestrated with Kubernetes, four control-plane procedures
key_result: Uses up to 34-55% less compute than stateful and stateless baselines, at least 40% less signalling, and completes complex procedures up to 50% faster.
limitation_or_critique: Evaluates efficiency and latency, not failover time or behaviour when the shared state store fails or is replicated across sites.

title: Estimating 5G Network Service Resilience Against Short Timescale Traffic Variation
authors: Rui Li; Bertrand Decocq; Anne Barros; Yi-Ping Fang; Zhiguo Zeng
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
summary: Builds a model of a virtualised 5G network that couples traffic dynamics with management mechanisms such as auto-scaling, to estimate how resilient each service is to short bursts of abnormal traffic.
method: analytical/simulation resilience model of traffic variation and management reactions
key_result: Quantifies service-level resilience under traffic surges and compares auto-scaling and isolation strategies, offering guidance for deployment and configuration.
limitation_or_critique: Simulation-only and focused on traffic surges; it does not cover NF or database failures or validate the model against a running core.

title: Enabling emerging edge applications through a 5G control plane intervention
authors: Mukhtiar Ahmad; Muhammad Ali Nawazish; Muhammad Taimoor Tariq; Muhammad Basit Iqbal Awan; Muhammad Taqi Raza; Zafar Ayyub Qazi
venue: Proceedings of the 18th International Conference on emerging Networking EXperiments and Technologies
summary: Proposes CellClone, an edge-based control plane that runs several active clones of control-plane functions with a quorum consistency protocol to mask faults and stragglers.
method: active replication with a custom low-latency quorum consistency protocol
data_or_testbed: testbed replaying real cellular control traces
key_result: Speeds up control-plane operations by a median of over 3.8x under node failures and stragglers and cuts missed application deadlines by over 90%.
limitation_or_critique: Redesigns the control plane rather than using 3GPP restoration; replication cost and geo-distributed deployment are not evaluated against standard UDSF-based designs.
